_comment: Hand-review corrections to the rule-based labeller, produced by reading every
one of the 165 archived media statements (headline + body) and comparing the
rule output against it. Each entry records WHY the human disagreed.
Positive class (`INCIDENT`) = the operator reports an UNPLANNED event that
degraded, halted or closed a NAMED rail/BRT line or station. Follow-up
updates and restoration notices for such an event count as the same class.
Everything else is excluded and reported separately: PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE
(works, tests, migrations, closures announced in advance) and NON_INCIDENT
(corporate, campaign, event, tender, policy, bus-route changes, retrospective
The rules get 138/165 right on their own; these 27 overrides are the residue.

`sameEventAs` links a later statement to an earlier one about the same real-world event. Both statements stay in the corpus because the pipeline should have flagged both; the report counts distinct events from this field. It does NOT remove entries from recall.

overrides.note: Rule said NON_INCIDENT because the body mentions card payment refunds. It is an apology for a real KGL disruption: train 22 failed near Phileo Damansara, single-track working to Semantan.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on a closing-paragraph phrase ('berjalan lancar'). Headline and body report a train stranded at Phileo Damansara.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on a weak marker. It is a substantive response about MRT Kajang service and the bridging buses during a disruption.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on 'PEMBUKAAN SEMULA PERKHIDMATAN'. Body reports train 59 withdrawn at Jelatek after a mechanical fault at 08:19 and crowding at KLCC.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. Body reports train 59's brake alarm activating at 20:26 near Kampung Baru, 500 passengers evacuated, train stranded at KL Sentral.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT because the body mentions 'pembayaran'. Real dual-line disruption: signal failure between Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara at 07:14.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on 'BERJALAN LANCAR'. It is a service update during the Bandaraya viaduct closure, i.e. the same unplanned disruption.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on 'SIASATAN MENYELURUH'. It reports the ongoing suspension of AG/PH service between Masjid Jamek and Bandaraya after the viaduct cracked.
Duplicate-version file of the 1 Feb 2023 investigation update; same unplanned Bandaraya viaduct disruption.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on 'SIASATAN ... SELESAI'. It states service was suspended between Masjid Jamek and Bandaraya since 27 Jan 2023 — a real disruption.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. Trains withdrawn from service and headway cut to 12 min because the Bandaraya structure and track are damaged — a service degradation, not a planned change.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. This is a scheduled suspension announced in advance (starts 2 April 2023) to allow repairs, so it belongs in PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE, not the unplanned-incident set.
Rule said INCIDENT. The statement extends peak-hour operating hours; it asserts no new service failure.
Follow-up on the Ampang corridor disruption. Issue type restated to the underlying cause (damaged structure at Bandaraya) rather than the bus-bridging subject of the release.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT and that is right: despite the 'pembukaan semula' context it is a ridership-target announcement, not a report of a service failure.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. Through-running restored after the Bandaraya closure — a restoration notice for the same unplanned disruption.
Kept as INCIDENT; issue type pinned to SIGNAL_FAULT because the lightning strike damaged the signalling system, which is the fault, not the weather.
Rule said PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE because the body mentions repair works. The headline is 'GANGGUAN SUIS LANDASAN' — an unplanned track-switch failure, and the works are the response to it.
Rule said PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE because of 'KERJA-KERJA BAIK PULIH'. The works are the response to an unplanned water-ingress track failure at 10:20 between Wangsa Maju and Sri Rampai.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT on 'PEMBAYARAN'. A tree fell on the monorail track at 14:20 near Raja Chulan; no service between KL Sentral and Medan Tuanku.

Rule said NON_INCIDENT. KLCC station closed to entering passengers after smoke was detected in the electronics room on 2 Jan 2025. No matching IssueType exists in the frozen enum (there is no FIRE/SMOKE member), so UNKNOWN is recorded rather than forcing a wrong label.
Restoration notice for the 2 Jan 2025 KLCC closure. Same reasoning on UNKNOWN issue type.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. A restoration notice ('kembali pulih') for a KGL disruption.
Rule said PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE. A restoration notice for a KJ disruption, not a planned works notice.
Rule got the class right but chose VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN; the statement says 'kerosakan teknikal pada landasan' — a track fault at PWTC at 09:58.

Rule chose ELEVATOR_FAULT from the phrase 'lif, eskalator dan lampu tidak dapat berfungsi', but the cause is a traction/substation power-supply failure across five underground stations at 19:50. The frozen enum has no POWER member, so UNKNOWN is the honest label.
Rule said NON_INCIDENT. It is a rescheduling of planned signalling upgrade works, so it belongs in PLANNED_SERVICE_CHANGE.

Rule said INCIDENT with MR+BRT. It is a genuine flood-driven outage but names 68 BUS routes, not a rail or BRT line, so it falls outside the positive class. Recorded here so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
Restoration statement for the same 6 Mar 2023 Kelana Jaya power-supply disruption.
